title: A few months into AI game development. Didn't expect to get this far
author: Appropriate_Number27
selftext:
Hi everyone,

So a few months back I decided to give it a shot. I don't have any game dev experience, but I do have some coding experience. In the past, I tried making a UE5 game by myself using tutorials, but I spent so much time just creating basic functionalities that I never really pursued it. Lately, I've been watching some of your posts and was amazed by your results, so I decided to try it myself.

To be honest, I wasn't expecting to get this far. I started this out of curiosity and was really amazed by how well it works. Most of my work is AI-generated. I've used free assets, and some of them I generated myself. Since this was just a personal project, I decided I didn't want to spend any money on assets.

I've been using Claude and ChatGPT. Previously, I was mainly using ChatGPT and Codex, but many of you suggested Opus and oh boy, were you right. Right now I'm considering switching completely to Claude, as I see much better quality and, most importantly, token efficiency. I haven't run the numbers exactly, but using Codex now feels like I'm working 10x slower compared to Claude. I'm also using Unreal MCP and Blender MCP.

I've created a zombie survival game (I know, very original, but I've always liked those games and, like many of you, I started creating a game that I would actually like to play myself).

It's a wave-based survival game with unlocks and building. You play, unlock stronger weapons, structures, traps and upgrades, and try to survive as many waves as possible. I've created two modes: one standard mode where you have some checkpoints and can start from wave 11 (if you've completed wave 15), and a second one called Hell Mode, where enemies are stronger and there are more of them. There's also a simple leaderboard.

My idea was to create a lightweight game that you can just open and play without having to invest too much time or focus.

This is definitely not a promotional post, as I don't even have a Steam page or anything like that. I just wanted to share my story and ask whether you think this game might be worth polishing and eventually releasing someday (in the very distant future). For now, it's just a prototype I made for fun.

To be honest, it still feels surreal to me, and if you have any tips on optimizing game development with AI, I'd really appreciate them.
